name: fish
description:
Inclusion Criteria

Laws and official materials about the catching, trade, import, export, production, processing, management, marketing and labelling of fish, shellfish and fish-derived products. This includes seafood products from wild-caught, freshwater, harvested, aquaculture and farmed sources; live shellfish intended for human consumption; processed fish products used as human food or animal feed; and fish by-products used in food, beverage or feed production.

Treat a source as in scope where its operative focus is commercial or regulatory control of fish, shellfish, seafood, fishery products, aquaculture or fish-derived food/feed/beverage products. Include import, export, trade, catching, landing, production, processing, management, marketing, labelling, traceability, live shellfish for human consumption, aquaculture and farmed-fish production, fish reared from roe, wild-caught fish later fattened in captivity, fishmeal, fish flour, fish pellets, milled fish products, caviar and fish by-products such as isinglass used in brewing or food processing.

Inclusion tests — keep in scope when the source:

- Regulates commercial catching, landing, sale or marketing of fish or shellfish
- Regulates import, export, certification, traceability or border control of fish, shellfish, seafood or fishery products
- Regulates aquaculture, fish farms, farmed fish, fish hatcheries, fish reared from roe, or wild-caught fish subsequently fattened in captivity
- Regulates processing, labelling, presentation, hygiene, marketing standards or production of fish or shellfish for human consumption
- Regulates fish-derived food, feed or beverage-production materials such as fishmeal, fish flour, fish pellets, caviar, fish oil for food/feed, fish bladders or isinglass

Borderline guidance (lean toward inclusion when materially relevant):

- IUU fishing and catch-certificate rules where they regulate commercial fish imports, exports, landings, traceability or trade
- Shellfish disease, live bivalve mollusc and harvesting-area rules linked to human consumption, trade, production, harvesting, processing or marketing
- Aquatic animal health rules that materially regulate aquaculture, farmed fish, live shellfish for consumption, seafood movements or fish production
- Animal by-product rules where fish-derived food/feed/beverage products or named fish by-products are materially covered
- General fisheries-management sources governing commercial catching, landing, quota-linked commercial management, sale or seafood supply

High-Priority Keyword Matches

fish, seafood, shellfish, fishery products, aquaculture, fish farming, fish import, fish export, fish trade, fish marketing, fish labelling, fish traceability, catch certificate, IUU fishing, live bivalve molluscs, fishmeal, fish flour, caviar, isinglass, fish processing, farmed fish.
exclusion_criteria:
Exclusion Criteria

We are not interested in the following:

- Ornamental aquatic species and ornamental fish kept for aquariums
- Aquarium fish and aquarium trade materials where the fish are not for human food, animal feed, aquaculture production, or food or beverage processing
- Fish kept as pets or pet-fish movements, welfare or trade
- Fish used for scientific research, laboratory testing or research-establishment purposes only
- Recreational fishing, sport fishing, angling, rod licences, leisure fishing permits and similar non-commercial fishing activities
- Fish conservation, biodiversity, habitat protection, species protection or ecological restoration materials where the operative purpose is conservation rather than catching, production, trade, marketing, food/feed use or aquaculture management
- Fish-derived products intended for non-food, non-feed and non-beverage uses, including cosmetics, personal care products, medical products, wound dressings, cosmetic collagen, industrial collagen and other industrial applications
- General marine environment, water quality, river basin, harbour, vessel safety or navigation materials unless they directly regulate fish, shellfish, aquaculture, seafood products, fishery products, fish-derived food/feed products, or commercial catching and landing
- General animal by-product materials unless they specifically concern fish, shellfish, fishery products, fishmeal, fish flour, fish oil, fish bladders, isinglass, caviar or other fish-derived products within the included food/feed/beverage scope

Exclude when the source is only about:

- Ornamental, aquarium or pet fish
- Recreational fishing, sport fishing, angling or leisure permits
- Scientific research use of fish
- Conservation, biodiversity, species protection or habitat restoration without material commercial, product, aquaculture or seafood controls
- Non-food fish-derived products such as cosmetics, personal care products, medical products, wound dressings or industrial collagen

keep: Catch certificates and export health certificates for fishery products
Import rules for fish, shellfish, seafood and fishery products (BTOM, IPAFFS, border control)
Aquaculture permits, fish-farm licensing and farmed-fish production
Fishmeal, fish flour and fish-derived feed import controls
Live bivalve mollusc harvesting-area and shellfish hygiene rules for human consumption
IUU fishing and commercial landing or traceability rules
drop: Ornamental aquarium fish and pet-fish trade only
Rod licences, angling and recreational or sport fishing permits
Fish habitat restoration or conservation with no commercial seafood controls
Fish mentioned only in passing on a general environment or water-quality page
